thought.text: System dependencies installed. Now let me install Node 24 and Ruby 3.4.9.

reasoning_content:
System deps installed. PostgreSQL and Redis installed. Now install Node 24 and Ruby 3.4.9. Let me use nodesource for Node 24, and for Ruby I'll build from source or use ruby-install. Let me do both in parallel-ish.

Actually let me check if there's a way to get Ruby 3.4 easily. Ubuntu 22.04 has Ruby 3.0. I'll build from source. Let me download ruby 3.4.9 source.

Let me start Ruby build (long) and Node install. I'll run them in one command sequentially but with output tail.

Actually building Ruby from source takes several minutes. Let me do it in background or just run it (600s timeout). Let's try.

First Node 24 install via nodesource.

action.command:
set -e
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x -o /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
bash /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh >/tmp/node_setup.log 2>&1
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq nodejs >/tmp/node_install.log 2>&1
node --version
npm --version
corepack --version 2>/dev/null || echo "no corepack"
